transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-21
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~45m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), David Ramos (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Borealis Head of ML), Samir Patel (CTO), Ava Nguyen (Engineer)

Summary (auto-gen, may be imperfect):
Borealis currently uses OpenAI for most generation and embeddings. They're evaluating Dedicated Redwood to bring costs down and control latency for latency-sensitive features. They run both chat and long-form completions, use function calls, and have some on-prem constraints for PII. Key ask: how close are Redwood-managed models to OpenAI's output (eval parity), what changes if we self-host weights via vLLM/TGI, and what the dedicated sizing & pricing looks like.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood, i have Dave with me, he's our SE, hi Dave.
[00:06] David Ramos: hey hi, good to meet you all.
[00:08] Lena Ortiz: hi, thanks for doing this. quick note, we might jump in and out — Samir has another meeting later — but we wanted to get the high-level map.
[00:15] Maya Chen: totally. quick round robin — can you share a bit about what you're running today and why you're looking to move off OpenAI hosted?
[00:25] Samir Patel: yeah, so we've been primarily on OpenAI for about 18 months. we like the model quality but cost has ramped — embeddings and chat tokens are our biggest spend. also the p50 latency for some of our user-facing helpers is spiky, and we want more control for compliance reasons.
[00:40] Ava Nguyen: also seeing some throttles during spikes; we want predictable throughput for support hours.
[00:45] David Ramos: okay that makes sense. are you doing any on-prem or private data handling that requires a VPC or customer-managed keys?
[00:52] Lena Ortiz: yes, some of our classification and PII redaction pipelines have to live in a private network; ideally we'd keep the control plane managed but have model runtime in our VPC or into a dedicated cluster.
[01:05] Maya Chen: cool — Redwood supports Hosted, Dedicated (reserved GPU pools), and Private with a VPC. Dedicated usually hits that sweet spot where teams get predictable throughput and cost savings vs public hosted. quick Q: are you using any custom finetunes or very recent OpenAI endpoints?
[01:20] Samir Patel: some fine-tunes, mostly prompt engineering. our biggest tech question is eval parity — if we move to Dedicated using the open models or to self-hosted weights with vLLM/TGI, can we get the exact same outputs?
[01:32] David Ramos: right — that's a common question. short answer: exact parity with a closed provider's finetuned endpoint is often not 1:1; there are determinism and pre/post-processing differences. but you can get very close; we do systematic evals to measure quality delta and have rollback/fallback policies.
[01:48] Lena Ortiz: what about things like function calling? we rely on structured outputs for our assistant, if the model behavior shifts it breaks downstream parsers.
[01:56] David Ramos: we support streaming and function/tool calling semantics. for Dedicated we run the same inference runtime with the same tokenization and function-call handling. differences usually show up if you change model checkpoint or quantization — e.g., switching from fp16 to 4-bit quant can shift outputs.
[02:15] Ava Nguyen: we've been experimenting with vLLM in-house for some high throughput scoring; the ops team likes TGI too. are those compatible if we bring our own weights?
[02:24] Maya Chen: yes, customers bring weights in vLLM or TGI formats frequently. Redwood supports common model formats and can route requests to compatible runtimes. the nuance is kernel selection and kv cache handling — we'll need to validate the same attention behavior, especially for long context.
[02:40] Samir Patel: attention behavior — can you expand? we saw some drift when moving from OpenAI to some OSS checkpoints in our internal tests.
[02:47] David Ramos: sure — two things: chunking/position embedding handling, and how kv cache is serialized across requests. some OSS kernels implement rotary or absolute positions slightly differently. we run a compatibility pass and recommend a small eval suite to detect regressions.
[03:02] Lena Ortiz: great. on the cost side, do you have ballpark reductions switching to Dedicated?
[03:07] Maya Chen: it depends on utilization; typical ranges we see are 30-60% lower per-token cost for steady high volume as you amortize the GPU pool. but you trade some flexibility — Dedicated has reserved capacity and burst policies.
[03:20] Samir Patel: and autoscaling? can it spin up for traffic spikes?
[03:24] David Ramos: yes, there are configurable autoscaling policies and burst capacity for sudden spikes. for hard SLOs we recommend setting headroom in the pool and a fallback routing policy to hosted or smaller models to avoid errors.
[03:36] Ava Nguyen: security — is Redwood SOC2? how do KMS and audit logs work?
[03:41] Maya Chen: Redwood is SOC2 compliant; we offer customer-managed KMS integrations, HSM options for Private, and per-request audit logs exported to your logging bucket. we can send the security pack after this call.
[03:53] Samir Patel: we'll need an inventory for legal — encryption in transit and at rest, RBAC, SSO.
[03:58] Maya Chen: yep will include in the security deck.
[04:01] Lena Ortiz: about eval parity — what does the validation flow look like?
[04:05] David Ramos: we typically do a three-step: 1) baseline run: run your existing prompt set and capture OpenAI outputs 2) parity run on Redwood Dedicated with same prompts + same temperature/seeds where possible, capture diffs and metrics (BLEU/ROUGE/embedding similarity) 3) tune: if you want, we can test quantization profiles and model variants, and generate a regression report. the goal is to measure delta and assess if it's within acceptable thresholds.
[04:28] Ava Nguyen: do you need us to provide prompts and sample logs?
[04:30] Maya Chen: yes, a representative prompt set (50-100) and examples of where current outputs break is ideal. we'll run an automated diff and then manual spot checks.
[04:39] Samir Patel: what's the pilot timeline look like?
[04:42] Maya Chen: most pilots are 2–4 weeks: initial setup and connectivity (aws/VPC/KMS), a 1-week baseline/bench run, and 1 week of tuning & report. we can compress if you have narrow scope.
[04:55] Lena Ortiz: sounds good. one more — what about embeddings migration? we use embeddings heavily for search; migrating vectors is non-trivial.
[05:03] David Ramos: for embeddings we provide conversion recommendations; often you'll reindex using the chosen model. Redwood can host the same open embedding model you used or recommend an equivalent. we'll include guidance on similarity thresholds and reindex cost estimates.
[05:18] Ava Nguyen: reindex cost — can you give a rough idea? reindexing ~50M docs is expensive.
[05:23] Maya Chen: yeah that's a scale conversation; options include incremental reindex, hybrid routing (some queries to OpenAI during migration), or running embeddings offline and bulk uploading. we'll put a cost/ops estimate into the sizing worksheet.
[05:36] Samir Patel: operationally, do we maintain the same SDK calls? we want minimal dev changes.
[05:40] David Ramos: the Redwood API is similar to other hosted APIs — REST/SDKs for text, chat, embeddings; we also have a migration guide and client libs. for function calling we support the same shape, but you may need small prompt/response parsing tweaks if outputs differ.
[05:55] Lena Ortiz: what's the worst-case — if parity is poor, can we fall back to OpenAI for certain routes?
[06:00] Maya Chen: yes, smart routing is a core feature — policy-based routing by route, latency, or cost. you can route critical endpoints to Hosted OpenAI or Redwood Hosted while others hit Dedicated. automatic fallback is supported.
[06:12] Ava Nguyen: about bringing our own weights: if we host a model in TGI on-prem, can Redwood's control plane still orchestrate?
[06:20] David Ramos: for Private deployments yes; the control plane can manage policies and metrics while runtime remains customer-managed. there are connectivity/agent requirements for metrics and logs. we'll document exact network and agent specs.
[06:33] Samir Patel: okay smart.
[06:35] Maya Chen: i'll summarize next steps: we'll send Dedicated sizing & pricing; David will send a benchmark plan; customer to send prompt set. we also agreed to share the security pack and a sample SOW template.
[06:47] Lena Ortiz: that works. can we also get a sample results dashboard?
[06:50] David Ramos: yep, we'll include sample dashboards for latency/cost and the parity report template.
[06:55] Samir Patel: one quick nit — we use both chat completions and long form generation, context windows can go to 32k for some docs. any limitations there?
[07:03] Maya Chen: Dedicated supports larger contexts depending on GPU selection; we'll propose a sizing that supports 32k. some quantization profiles affect max context, so we'll call that out.
[07:15] Ava Nguyen: thanks. last thing, SLA — do you have latency SLAs or uptime guarantees for Dedicated?
[07:20] Maya Chen: Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and latency targets in enterprise contracts. we'll surface the SLA language in the SOW.
[07:28] Lena Ortiz: ok great. thanks everyone.
[07:30] Maya Chen: thanks all — we'll follow up with the materials and schedule the pilot kickoff.
